Campus Customs – App Check

Problem 11 · screenshots from the real running app (React + Vite frontend, FastAPI + PydanticAI backend)

Test 1 · Chat + database

The chatbot answers an inventory question with the correct price and stock

Asked “how much is the benjamin franklin 1 4 zip?”, the assistant replied “The Benjamin Franklin 1/4 Zip is $72.00.” — the exact price stored in campus_customs.db. This proves the agent looks product data up in the database and quotes the real price instead of making one up.

Test 2 · Chat → page

Dynamic product cards appear on the page after a chat search

Asking “what t-shirts do you have?” in the chat populated a “From the chat” band on the page with real product cards (image, type, name, description, price) — the same cards as the Products page, including a “Low stock” badge. This proves the backend returns structured product data and the React frontend renders it; clicking any card opens that product's detail page.

Test 3 · Usability (Problem 9)

Improved product search & filtering

On the Products page, the new Sort control (set here to Price: high to low), the In stock only toggle, and the category chips let shoppers reorder and narrow the catalogue — here the most expensive items (the $98 jackets) come first. This proves the Problem 9 search/filtering improvement works and helps shoppers find what they want faster.
